```{r}
#| label: setup


# Source figure options, packages, and main data prep.
source("./R/fig-opt-fun.R")
source("./R/packages.R")
source("./R/data-prep.R")
source("./R/helpers.R")
source("./R/sim-fun.R")


refit.models <- FALSE


# Functions  ################################################################


# Text formatting for inline reporting. Use the full version at first
# mention, e.g. `r ctxt$TG_T4` -> "-9% (95% CrI: -20, +3%; P(benefit) 93%)",
# and the short version thereafter, e.g. `r ctxt_simple$TG_T4` ->
# "-9% (-20, +3%; P(benefit) 93%)"
fmt_prob <- function(p) {
  case_when(p > 0.99 ~ ">99%",
            p < 0.01 ~ "<1%",
            .default = paste0(round(100 * p), "%"))
}


```


Here, we draw inferences about the effect of krill oil supplementation on metabolic health markers. First, we examine the differences in outcomes between placebo and krill oil, followed by a combined analysis of the dichotomous diagnostic score (0/1) and a continuous version derived from the sum of the sub-scores, each given equal weight.


```{r}
#| label: load-data


# Creates labels, loads data and models.
dat <- data_load_s7s10()


# Create a data set for labelling types. Built from the scale slot returned
# by data_load_s7s10(), type index matches the Stan data. Units
# are checked against the AOData package documentation (?bloodvar, ?glucose,
# ?waist_bp, ?bodycomp). BMI and relative fat mass are derived in
# data-prep.R from DXA body mass (kg) and height (m).
labels <- dat$scale |> 
  select(type, analyte) |> 
  mutate(label = case_when(
           analyte == "HDL" ~ "High density lipoprotein", 
           analyte == "LDL" ~ "Low density lipoprotein", 
           analyte == "glucose" ~ "Fasting glucose", 
           analyte == "TG" ~ "Triglycerides", 
           analyte == "waist" ~ "Waist circumference", 
           analyte == "sys" ~ "Systolic blood pressure", 
           analyte == "dias" ~ "Diastolic blood pressure", 
           analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "Relative fat mass", 
           analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "HOMA2-IR", 
           analyte == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index", 
           analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "Adiponectin",
           analyte == "HbA1c" ~ "HbA1c",
           .default = analyte
         ),
         unit = case_when(
           analyte %in% c("HDL", "LDL", "TG", "glucose") ~ "mmol/L",
           analyte %in% c("sys", "dias") ~ "mmHg",
           analyte == "waist" ~ "cm",
           analyte == "bmi" ~ "kg/m^2",
           analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "%",
           analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "mg/L",
           analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "index (unitless)",
           analyte == "HbA1c" ~ "mmol/mol",
           .default = NA_character_
         )) |> 
  arrange(type)


# For re-running the models
d <- dat$d


# Compile relevant models. 
# S18 is the univariate t model. Used for sensitivity check, 
# what is the effect of multivariate on inference.
s18 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/s18.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/s18.exe")

# S13 is the preffered main model, multivariate t distribution.
s13 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/s13.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/s13.exe")


# Fit model (get posterior distributions) 
fit_wrap(s18, DATA = d, fit = "fit.s18.post")
fit_wrap(s13, DATA = d, fit = "fit.s13.post")


```


```{r}
#| label: infer-fig-data-prep


  
# Observed data on the natural scale (all available observations)
obs_dat <- criteria_dat |>

  select(participant, time, treat, sex, analyte, value) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  inner_join(labels, by = "analyte") |>
  inner_join(dat$scale |> select(type, transform), by = "type") |>
  mutate(treat = factor(treat, levels = c("ctrl", "omega"),
                        labels = c("Placebo", "Krill oil")))

# Observed group means. Geometric means for the log-transformed outcomes
# (TG, HOMA2IR, HbA1c) so that they are comparable with the back-transformed model
# estimates, arithmetic means otherwise.
obs_means <- obs_dat |>
  summarise(.by = c(type, analyte, label, unit, time, treat),
            Mu = if_else(first(transform) == "log", exp(mean(log(value))), mean(value)),
            n = n())   |> 
  mutate(
     unit = case_when(
           analyte %in% c("HDL", "LDL", "TG", "glucose") ~ "mmol&times;L<sup>-1</sup>", 
           analyte %in% c("sys", "dias") ~ "mmHg", 
           analyte == "waist" ~ "cm", 
           analyte == "bmi" ~ "kg&times;m<sup>-2</sup>", 
           analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "%", 
           analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "mg&times;L<sup>-1</sup>", 
           analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "index",
           analyte == "HbA1c" ~ "mmol&times;mol<sup>-1</sup>",
           .default = NA_character_
         ))

# Covariate values for adjusted means
# Pre-intervention covariate: overall mean of the standardised baseline value
# per type (the same value for both groups gives adjusted group means). Sex is
# coded -0.5/0.5, so sex = 0 gives the average over sexes and the beta_sex
# term (s13 and s18) drops out of the linear predictor.
pre_means <- dat$dat |>
  filter(pre_miss == 1) |>
  distinct(P, type, pre_obs) |>
  summarise(.by = type, pre = mean(pre_obs))

# Model-based adjusted means, back-transformed to the natural scale
# alpha[time, type, treat] are time-specific intercepts, beta[type, time] the
# pre-value slopes; mu = alpha + beta * pre on the standardised scale.
predict_means <- function(fit, model) {

  alpha <- fit$draws("alpha", format = "df") |>
    select(.draw, starts_with("alpha")) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = -.draw, values_to = "alpha") |>
    mutate(name = gsub("alpha\\[|\\]", "", name)) |>
    separate(name, into = c("time", "type", "treat"), sep = ",", convert = TRUE)

  beta <- fit$draws("beta", format = "df") |>
    select(.draw, starts_with("beta")) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = -.draw, values_to = "beta") |>
    mutate(name = gsub("beta\\[|\\]", "", name)) |>
    separate(name, into = c("type", "time"), sep = ",", convert = TRUE)

  alpha |>
    inner_join(beta, by = c(".draw", "time", "type")) |>
    inner_join(pre_means, by = "type") |>
    mutate(mu = alpha + beta * pre) |>
    summarise(.by = c(time, type, treat),
              # We use the median here
              Mu = median(mu),
              lwr95 = quantile(mu, 0.025),
              upr95 = quantile(mu, 0.975),
              lwr50 = quantile(mu, 0.25),
              upr50 = quantile(mu, 0.75)) |>
    # Back-transform (monotone, so quantiles map directly)
    inner_join(dat$scale, by = "type") |>
    mutate(across(c(Mu, lwr95, upr95, lwr50, upr50),
                  ~ if_else(transform == "log", exp(mean + sd * .x), mean + sd * .x))) |>
    mutate(time = if_else(time == 1, "T2", "T4"),
           treat = factor(treat, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Placebo", "Krill oil")),
           model = model) |>
    select(model, time, type, analyte, treat, Mu, lwr95, upr95, lwr50, upr50)
}

pred_means <- bind_rows(
  predict_means(fit.s13.post, "s13")
) |>
  inner_join(labels, by = c("type", "analyte")) 





# We are creating two plots, one for the metabolic syndrom subscores

strip_lab <- function(label, unit) paste0(label, " (", unit, ")")

pred_plot_dat <- pred_means |>
  
   mutate(

           analyte == "bmi" ~ "kg&times;m<sup>-2</sup>",

           analyte == "HbA1c" ~ "mmol&times;mol<sup>-1</sup>",

         ),

                                          "dias",

                                          "TG",
                                          "bmi",
                                          "fat.rel",

                                          "Adiponectin",

         strip.lab = strip_lab(label, unit),
         # Facet strips follow the order of the analyte levels

pred_plot <- function(dat,obs, analytes) {
  

  # Position 
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.1)
  
  
  
  obs_means <- obs |>
    filter(analyte %in% analytes) |>
    # Same factor levels as dat so both layers share the panel order
    mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = levels(dat$analyte))) |> 
     mutate(time = factor(time, labels = c("Baseline", "Supplementation", 
                                          "Combined"))) 

  # Strip labels keyed by analyte
  strip_labels <- dat |>
    distinct(analyte, strip.lab) |>
    with(setNames(as.character(strip.lab), analyte))

  
  dat |> 
    mutate(time = factor(time, labels = c("Supplementation", 
                                          "Combined"))) |> 
    # Filter based on analyte
  filter(analyte %in% analytes) |> 
    
  ggplot(aes(time, Mu, color = treat, group = interaction(treat, model))) +

  # Observed means at all time-points (descriptive)
  geom_point(data = obs_means,
             aes(time, Mu, color = treat, group = treat),
             shape = 1, size = 1.5,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_line(data = obs_means,
            aes(time, Mu, color = treat, group = treat),
            linetype = "dotted",
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +

  # Model-based adjusted means at T2 and T4
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr95, ymax = upr95), width = 0, linewidth = 0.4, position = pd) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr50, ymax = upr50), width = 0, linewidth = 1.1, position = pd) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = treat), size = 1.5, color = "black", position = pd, shape = 21) +

  facet_wrap(~ analyte, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1,
             labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(4, 2)]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colscale[c(4, 2)]) +
    scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge=2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
    
  # scale_shape_manual(values = c(s18 = 24, s13 = 21)) +
  alpha_theme() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  
  theme(strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(), 
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        legend.title = element_blank()) +
  
  labs(x = "Time-point",
       y = "Outcome (natural scale)",
       color = "Treatment", fill = "Treatment")
    
  
  
  
}
  




# Metabolic syndrome subscores
met_sym_scores <- pred_plot(pred_plot_dat, 
                            obs_means, 
                            analytes = c("HDL", "glucose", "TG", "waist", "sys", "dias"))

# Related scores
rel_scores <- pred_plot(pred_plot_dat,
                            obs_means,
                            analytes = c("fat.rel", "Adiponectin", "HOMA2IR",
                                         "bmi", "LDL", "HbA1c"))


## Add the contrats plot 
draws.s18 <- fit.s18.post$draws("alpha", format = "df")
draws.s13 <- fit.s13.post$draws("alpha", format = "df")



ls <- list(s18 = draws.s18, 
           s13 = draws.s13)

infer_treat <- function(draws_list, scale = dat$scale) {
  
  models <- names(draws_list)
  
  contrasts <- list()
  estimates <- list()
  for (i in seq_along(models)) {
  
    estimates[[i]] <- draws_list[[i]] |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("alpha")) |> 
  mutate(name = gsub("alpha\\[|\\]", "", name)) |> 
  
  separate(name, into = c("time", "type", "treat"))  |> 
    mutate(treat = if_else(treat == 1, "ctrl", "omega")) |> 
    mutate(model = models[i])
  
  
  # Contrast on the standardised scale (alpha is the intercept at pre = 0 and
  # sex = 0, and there is no treatment x pre interaction, so omega - ctrl is
  # the adjusted mean difference at any pre value). Back-transformation uses
  # the per-type sd from data_load_s7s10()$scale:
  # contrast_nat = sd * contrast  -> difference in natural units, or on the
  #                                   log scale for TG, HOMA2IR and HbA1c
  # ratio = exp(sd * contrast) -> krill oil / placebo ratio (log outcomes
  #                                   only; NA otherwise)
  contrasts[[i]] <- estimates[[i]] |> 
    pivot_wider(names_from = treat, 
                values_from = value) |> 
    mutate(contrast = omega - ctrl) |> 
    mutate(type = as.integer(type)) |> 
    inner_join(scale |> select(type, analyte, transform, sd), by = "type") |> 
    mutate(contrast_nat = sd * contrast, 
           ratio = if_else(transform == "log", exp(contrast_nat), NA_real_)) |> 
    select(-sd) |> 
    mutate(model = models[i])
    
  }
  
  estimates <- bind_rows(estimates)
  contrasts <- bind_rows(contrasts)
  
  return(list(estimates = estimates, 
              contrasts = contrasts))
}

# Run the infear routine
infer <- infer_treat(ls)

   inner_join(labels, by = c("type", "analyte")) |>

           analyte %in% c("sys", "dias") ~ "mmHg",

           analyte == "bmi" ~ "kg&times;m<sup>-2</sup>", 
           analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "%", 
           analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "mg&times;L<sup>-1</sup>", 
           analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "Fold-difference",
           analyte == "HbA1c" ~ "Fold-difference",
           .default = NA_character_
         ),
     analyte = factor(analyte, levels = c("waist",
                                          "dias",
                                          "sys",
                                          "glucose",
                                          "HDL",
                                          "TG",
                                          "bmi",
                                          "fat.rel",
                                          "LDL",
                                          "Adiponectin",

                                          "HbA1c"))) |>
  mutate(strip.lab = strip_lab(label, unit),
         # Facet strips follow the order of the analyte levels
         strip.lab = fct_reorder(strip.lab, as.integer(analyte), .fun = min),
         contrast_out = if_else(transform == "log", ratio, contrast_nat), 
         # Add a no diff line (0 for natural scale and 1 for ratio (fold-difference))
         no_diff = if_else(analyte %in% c("TG", "HOMA2IR", "HbA1c"), 1, 0))
  

contrast_plot <- function(dat, analytes) {

}
```

```{r}
#| label: joint-burden-score

# Extract all alpha effects
a <- fit.s13.post$draws("alpha", format = "df")

# A function for getting the t:th time point and k:th effect from the matrix
# and contrasted between treatment groups (2 vs 1).
# the effect (eff) is then combined below.
eff <- function(t, k) a[[sprintf("alpha[%d,%d,2]", t, k)]] - a[[sprintf("alpha[%d,%d,1]", t, k)]]

# Combined posterior effect. The type index of each criterion is looked up
# from the data (dat$scale), matching diag_idx in s13.stan:
# HDL = 2, TG = 6, dias = 8, glucose = 10, sys = 11, waist = 12
type_idx <- setNames(dat$scale$type, dat$scale$analyte)

# The score is
# (0.5 * (dias + sys) +
# (- HDL) + TG + glucose + waist) / 5
burden_eff <- sapply(1:2, function(t)
    (-eff(t, type_idx[["HDL"]]) + eff(t, type_idx[["TG"]]) +
       0.5 * (eff(t, type_idx[["dias"]]) + eff(t, type_idx[["sys"]])) +
       eff(t, type_idx[["glucose"]]) + eff(t, type_idx[["waist"]])) / 5
  )

colnames(burden_eff) <- c("T2", "T4")

# Store burden contrast for text (see below)
burden_contrast <- burden_eff |> 
  data.frame()  |> 
  pivot_longer(everything()) |> 
    summarise(.by = c(name),
            # Median posterior w. 95% CrI on the reporting standardized scale
            # (sd units)
            med = median(value),
            # Density height at the median (same defaults as stat_density)
            dens_med = with(density(value), approx(x, y, xout = med)$y),
            lwr95 = quantile(value, 0.025),
            upr95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            # Proportion of posterior that shows benefit in treatment
            benefit = mean(value < 0))  |>
  mutate(
    digits = 2,
    unit_txt = "SD-units",
    est = sprintf("%.*f %s", digits, med, unit_txt),
    ci = sprintf("%.*f, %.*f", digits, lwr95, digits, upr95),
    prob = paste("P(benefit)", fmt_prob(benefit)),
    txt = sprintf("%s (95%% CrI: %s; %s)", est, ci, prob),
    txt_simple = sprintf("%s (%s; %s)", est, ci, prob),
    name = factor(name, levels = c("T2", "T4"), 
                       labels = c("Supplementation", 
                                  "Combined"))) 


burden_t2 <- burden_contrast |> 
  filter(name == "Supplementation") |> 
  pull(txt_simple)

burden_t4 <- burden_contrast |> 
  filter(name == "Combined") |> 
  pull(txt_simple)

## Burden figure 



burden_fig <- burden_eff |> 
  data.frame()  |> 

  pivot_longer(everything()) |> 
    mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("T2", "T4"), 
                       labels = c("Supplementation", 
                                  "Combined"))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(value, color = name)) +
  # Shade the part of each density indicating benefit (krill oil < placebo)
  geom_area(aes(y = after_stat(ifelse(x < 0, density, 0)), fill = name),
            stat = "density", color = NA, alpha = 0.3,
            position = "identity") +
  geom_line(stat = "density", alpha = 0.8, 
            show.legend = FALSE)   +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 2, color = "gray50") +
  
  geom_text(data = burden_contrast, 
            aes(x = med - 0.12, 
                y = dens_med, 
            label = prob), 
            show.legend = FALSE, 
            size = 6/.pt) +

  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE, text_base_size = 7) +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom", 
        legend.title = element_blank(), 
        legend.direction = "horizontal", 
        legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"))  +
  labs(color = "Treatment-period",
       fill = "Treatment-period",
       x = "Average burden score<br>Krill oil - Placebo (SD-units)") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = colscale[c(3,6)]) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(3,6)])
```

```{r}
#| label: diagnostic-criteria-analysis
#| 


# Create a data sets with treatment allocations
dat <- data_load_s7s10()


dobs <- dat$dat |> 
  distinct(P, treat) |> 
  expand_grid(time = c(1, 2, 3))


draws <- fit.s13.post$draws("diagnosed", format = "df")


infer_diagnosed <- function(draws, dobs, ndraws = 1000) {
  
  
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.15)
  
  dat_out <- draws |> 
    filter(.draw %in% sample(1:8000, ndraws)) |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("diagnosed")) |> 
    mutate(name = gsub("diagnosed\\[|\\]", "", name)) |> 
    separate(name, into = c("P", "time")) |> 
        mutate(P = as.integer(P), 
           time = as.integer(time)) |> 
    

    inner_join(dobs) |> 
    
    mutate(time = if_else(time == 1, "Baseline", 
                          if_else(time == 2, "Supplementation", "Combined")),
           time = factor(time, levels = c("Baseline", "Supplementation", "Combined")), 
           
           treat = if_else(treat == 1, "Placebo", "Krill oil"), 
           treat = factor(treat, levels = c("Placebo", "Krill oil"))) |> 
    
    summarise(.by = c(treat, time,.draw), 
              frac.diagnosed = 100 * (sum(value) / n())) |> 
    summarise(.by = c(treat, time), 
              m = median(frac.diagnosed), 
              lwr99 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.01), 
              lwr95 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.025), 
              lwr50 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.25), 
              upr50 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.75),
              upr95 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.975),
              upr99 = quantile(frac.diagnosed, 0.99)) 
    
  
  
  dat_out |> 
  
    ggplot(aes(time, m, 
               fill = as.factor(treat), 
               color = as.factor(treat),
               group = as.factor(treat))) + 
    

    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr95, 
                      ymax = upr95),
                  size = 0.4,
                  width = 0, 
                  position = pd) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr50, 
                      ymax = upr50),
                  size  = 1.5,
                  width = 0, 
                  position = pd) +
    
    geom_line(position = pd) + 
    
    geom_point(shape = 21, 
               size = 0.9, 
               color = "black",
                  position = pd) + 
    
  
    scale_fill_manual(values = colscale[c(4,2)]) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(4,2)]) +
        labs(y = "Diagnosis (%)") +
    
      alpha_theme(text_base_size = 7) + 
    
    theme(legend.position = "inside", 
          legend.position.inside = c(0.5, 0.9),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
          legend.title = element_blank(), 
          legend.key.height = unit(2, "mm"), 
          legend.background = element_blank())  +
      scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(n.dodge=2)) 
    
  
}
  

diagnosis_per_treat <- infer_diagnosed(draws, dobs, ndraws = 100)





# Using seqwrap to infer diagnosed fraction differences 
# between treatment groups. 
# Background: The diagnose criteria is a 0/1 variable built from 
# the sub-scores and thresholds associated with each score. It is difficult 
# to include a binary (threshold) quantity as a parameter in the Stan model. 
# A simpler alternative is to get the diagnosis in each MCMC iteration in the 
# generated quantities block and then model across a set of iterations.
# The standard errors of the per iteration model estimates needs to be combined 
# (see below) to get correct confidence intervals where imputation uncertainty
# and sampling uncertainty are both included.


# We will use the seqwrap package to model the diagnostic generated quantities
# across iterations. 
library(seqwrap)


draws.s13 <- fit.s13.post$draws("diagnosed", format = "df")
draws.s18 <- fit.s18.post$draws("diagnosed", format = "df")

# Create a data sets with treatment allocations
dat <- data_load_s7s10()

dobs <- dat$dat |> 
  distinct(P, treat) |> 
  expand_grid(time = c(1, 2, 3))



# A function for performing the seqwrap routine. 
infer_seqwrap <- function(draws, dobs, ndraws = 500) {
  
  
  # The variance co-variance eval function
  # Use this if creating a "joint test" 
  # We are skipping this now
   vcov_eval <- function(m) {
    V  <- vcov(m)$cond
    nm <- rownames(V)
    data.frame(row   = rep(nm, times = length(nm)),
               col   = rep(nm, each  = length(nm)),
               value = as.vector(V))
  }
  
  
   
   # Create metadata
  metadata <- draws |> 
    filter(.draw == 1) |> 
    # Re-name seq_sample_id
    select(.draw, starts_with("diagnosed")) |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("diag")) |> 
    mutate(name = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", name), 
         name = gsub(",", "_", name), 
         part_time = gsub("diagnosed", "", name)) |> 
  separate(part_time, into = c("P", "time")) |> 
     mutate(P = as.integer(P)) |> 
     inner_join( dobs |> 
                   distinct(P, treat)) |> 
     select(seq_sample_id = name, P, time, treat) |> 
       mutate(
         treat = paste0("treat", treat), 
         time = paste0("time", time))  
     

  # Data set 
  dat <- draws |> 
    slice_sample(n = ndraws) |> 
    # Re-name seq_sample_id
  select(.draw, starts_with("diagnosed")) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("diag")) |> 
  mutate(name = gsub("\\[|\\]", "", name), 
         name = gsub(",", "_", name)) |> 
  pivot_wider(values_from = value, names_from = name) 
  
  # Prepare and run seqwrap
  model <- seqwrap_compose(
    modelfun = glmmTMB::glmmTMB, 
    arguments = alist(
      formula = y ~ time * treat + (1|P), 
      family = stats::binomial, 
      # This adds weak priors on fixed effects parameters
      # in each run.
      priors = data.frame(prior = rep("normal(0,3)", 5), 
                                   class = rep("fixef", 5), 
                                   coef = c("timetime2", "timetime3", 
                                            "treattreat2", 
                                            "timetime2:treattreat2", 
                                            "timetime3:treattreat2")
        )
      ), 
    data = dat, 
    # eval_fun = vcov_eval,
    samplename = "seq_sample_id",
    metadata = metadata)
  
  results <- seqwrap(model, 
                       cores = 12)
  
  # Should return errors also
  sw_sums <- seqwrap_summarise(results)
  
  return(sw_sums)
  
}

# Rubin's Rule Pooling 
# see here for light introduction 
# https://metricgate.com/docs/rubins-rules-pooling/
# We want to pool variances from each imputed data set - 
# this will give uncertainties that reflect both imputation and 
# sampling uncertainty.

pool_rubin <- function(sums) {
    sums |>
      filter(term %in% c("timetime2:treattreat2", 
                         "timetime3:treattreat2")) |>
      summarise(.by = term,
                m    = n(),
                qbar = mean(estimate),    # This is the pooled estimate
                ubar = mean(std.error^2), # Within-impute variance
                b    = var(estimate)) |>  # between-impute variance
      mutate(
        # Total variance
        t = ubar + (1 + 1/m) * b,
        # "fraction of missing information"
        lambda = (1 + 1/m) * b / t,
       # Between impute var relative to within
        riv  = (1 + 1/m) * b / ubar,
         # DF calculation
        df = (m - 1) / lambda^2,
        se = sqrt(t), # Pooled SE
       # Confidence intervals (95%) and p-values
        lwr = qbar - qt(0.975, df) * se,
        upr = qbar + qt(0.975, df) * se,
        p = 2 * pt(-abs(qbar / se), df),
        or = exp(qbar), 
       or_lwr = exp(lwr), 
       or_upr = exp(upr))
  }


est_13 <- pool_rubin(sw_results13$summaries)
est_18 <- pool_rubin(sw_results18$summaries)

diag_criteria_fig <- est_13 |> 
  mutate(term = if_else(term == "timetime2:treattreat2", "Krill oil - Placebo\nSupplementation", 
                        "Krill oil - Placebo\nCombined treatment"), 
         term = factor(term, levels = c(
           "Krill oil - Placebo\nCombined treatment", 
           "Krill oil - Placebo\nSupplementation"))) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(term, qbar, color = term)) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr, 
                    ymax = upr), 
                width = 0,
                show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, 
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(3,6)] ) +
  alpha_theme(text_base_size = 7) + 
  
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "Log(OR) (&pm; 95% CI)") +
  
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2, color = "gray50") +
  coord_flip() + 

  theme(axis.title.x = ggtext::element_markdown())
```

```{r}
#| label: contrast-text

contrast_summary <- contrast_dat |>
  # Add a fix for direction of the effect, HDL and adiponectin are beneficial
  # when increased. A "unified" direction contrast:
  mutate(contrast_unif = if_else(analyte %in% c("Adiponectin","HDL"), -contrast, contrast),
         time = if_else(time == 1, "T2", "T4")) |>
  summarise(.by = c(analyte, time, transform),
            # Median posterior w. 95% CrI on the reporting scale (natural
            # units, or krill oil/placebo ratio for log outcomes)
            med = median(contrast_out),
            lwr95 = quantile(contrast_out, 0.025),
            upr95 = quantile(contrast_out, 0.975),
            # Proportion of posterior that shows benefit in treatment
            benefit = mean(contrast_unif < 0)) |>
  arrange(analyte, time)




ctxt_dat <- contrast_summary |>
  mutate(
    unit_txt = case_when(
      analyte %in% c("HDL", "LDL", "glucose") ~ "mmol/L",
      analyte %in% c("sys", "dias") ~ "mmHg",
      analyte == "waist" ~ "cm",
      analyte == "bmi" ~ "kg/m^2^",
      analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "%-points",
      analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "mg/L",
      .default = NA_character_),
    digits = if_else(analyte %in% c("sys", "dias", "waist", "fat.rel"), 1, 2),
    # Point estimate and interval bounds, ratios reported as percent
    # difference (krill oil vs. placebo)
    est = if_else(transform == "log",
                  sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (med - 1)),
                  sprintf("%.*f %s", digits, med, unit_txt)),
    ci = if_else(transform == "log",
                 sprintf("%+.0f, %+.0f%%", 100 * (lwr95 - 1), 100 * (upr95 - 1)),
                 sprintf("%.*f, %.*f", digits, lwr95, digits, upr95)),
    prob = paste("P(benefit)", fmt_prob(benefit)),
    txt = sprintf("%s (95%% CrI: %s; %s)", est, ci, prob),
    txt_simple = sprintf("%s (%s; %s)", est, ci, prob),
    key = paste(analyte, time, sep = "_"))

ctxt <- with(ctxt_dat, setNames(as.list(txt), key))
ctxt_simple <- with(ctxt_dat, setNames(as.list(txt_simple), key))


# Waist single values
waist_est_t2 <- ctxt_dat |> 
  filter(analyte == "waist", time == "T2") |> 
  mutate(stat = sprintf("%s (95%% PI: %s)", est, ci)) |> 
  pull(stat)

waist_prob_t2 <- ctxt_dat |> 
  filter(analyte == "waist", time == "T2") |> 
  mutate(stat = fmt_prob(benefit)) |> 
  pull(stat)





```




At post-supplementation (T2), baseline- and sex-adjusted differences between groups indicated a reduced waist circumference in krill oil compared to placebo `r waist_est_t2` with the probability of any benefit (proportion of the posterior density indicating benefit for the krill oil group, P(benefit)) being `r waist_prob_t2`. After the combined period (supplementation and resistance training), the between-group contrast for waist circumference indicated no difference, `r ctxt$waist_T4` (@fig-metsyn-inference). Both diastolic and systolic blood pressure indicated beneficial effects in krill oil compared to placebo at T2 (`r ctxt_simple$dias_T2` and `r ctxt_simple$sys_T2` for diastolic and systolic blood pressure, respectively). Although both the average diastolic and systolic blood pressure were more similar between krill oil and placebo after the second period, the probability distribution indicated a higher probability of benefit in the krill oil group (`r ctxt_simple$dias_T4` and `r ctxt_simple$sys_T4` for diastolic and systolic blood pressure, respectively; @fig-metsyn-inference).

After the supplementation period, the krill oil group displayed similar levels of high-density lipoproteins (HDL) as compared to the placebo group (`r ctxt_simple$HDL_T2`). However, following the combined period, the krill oil group increased HDL levels compared to placebo, indicating a higher probability of beneficial effects of krill oil supplementation (`r ctxt_simple$HDL_T4`). Triglyceride levels were estimated to be similar between intervention protocols, both after the post-supplementation period (`r ctxt_simple$TG_T2`) and after the combined period (`r ctxt_simple$TG_T4`).

A combined score was created by summing the five sub-scores of the metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria from their continuous, standardized scales, with each score given equal weight (the average blood pressure score was one-fifth of the total score). Comparing the combined scores between treatments indicated a high probability of benefit from krill oil at both post-treatment time points (post-supplementation, `r burden_t2`; post combined treatment, `r burden_t4`; @fig-metsyn-inference B). The differences in the combined score did not yield a significant (95% confidence interval not containing 0) difference in the dichotomous diagnostic criteria (harmonised definition, at least three of the five criteria passing their thresholds [@alberti2009]; @fig-metsyn-inference C and D).      



Comparing BMI between treatment groups indicated no clear difference between groups at follow-up time points (`r ctxt$bmi_T2` and `r ctxt_simple$bmi_T4`, for after the supplementation and combined periods, respectively). However, relative fat mass indicated a higher probability of an adverse effect of krill oil compared to placebo after the supplementation period (`r ctxt_simple$fat.rel_T2`). After the combined period, differences were smaller (`r ctxt_simple$fat.rel_T4`). Adjusted differences between groups in low density lipoprotein (LDL) and Adiponectin indicated similarity between treatments (LDL post-supplementation, `r ctxt_simple$LDL_T2`; LDL post-combined treatment, `r ctxt_simple$LDL_T4`; Adiponectin post-supplementation, `r ctxt_simple$Adiponectin_T2`; Adiponectin post-combined treatment `r ctxt_simple$Adiponectin_T4`). Insulin resistance, estimated using the HOMA2-IR model score, indicated a greater posterior probability of benefit at post-supplementation after krill oil compared to placebo (`r ctxt_simple$HOMA2IR_T2`), a difference that was not present after the combined time period (`r ctxt_simple$HOMA2IR_T4`). Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) was slightly higher in krill oil compared to placebo after the supplementation period, indicating a low probability of benefit (`r ctxt$HbA1c_T2`). After the combined period, the difference was smaller and more uncertain (`r ctxt_simple$HbA1c_T4`).

```{r}
#| label: between-type-correlations

# This is still work in progress. The residual correlations are correlations
# between variables at T2 and T4 and show correlations after accounting for 
# sex, treatment and pre-values. E.g., a positive correlation between sys and dia
# indicate that individuals with higher than expected diastolic 
# bp also tend to have have higher than expected systolic bp
# after acounting fort sex, pre-value and treatment.

 
# Residual correlation matrix Omega from s13 (M = 2K; rows/cols 1:K = T2,
# (K+1):M = T4). These are correlations conditional on treatment, baseline
# value and sex, i.e. how participants' deviations from their expected
# values co-vary between measurement types.
K <- dat$d$K

type_lab <- dat$scale |>
  distinct(type, analyte) |>
  arrange(type)

omega_draws <- fit.s13.post$draws("Omega", format = "df") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Omega")) |>
  mutate(name = gsub("Omega\\[|\\]", "", name)) |>
  separate(name, into = c("i", "j"), convert = TRUE) |>
  mutate(time_i = if_else(i <= K, "T2", "T4"),
         time_j = if_else(j <= K, "T2", "T4"),
         type_i = (i - 1) %% K + 1,
         type_j = (j - 1) %% K + 1)

omega_sum <- omega_draws |>
  summarise(.by = c(i, j, time_i, time_j, type_i, type_j),
            med = median(value),
            lwr95 = quantile(value, 0.025),
            upr95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            # Posterior probability of a positive correlation
            p_pos = mean(value > 0)) |>
  left_join(type_lab |> rename(type_i = type, analyte_i = analyte),
            by = "type_i") |>
  left_join(type_lab |> rename(type_j = type, analyte_j = analyte),
            by = "type_j")

# Within-time correlations between the burden score components
diag_types <- type_lab |>
  filter(analyte %in% c("HDL", "TG", "dias", "glucose", "sys", "waist")) |>
  pull(type)

omega_sum |>
  filter(time_i == time_j,
         type_i %in% diag_types, type_j %in% diag_types,
         type_i < type_j) |>
  select(time = time_i, analyte_i, analyte_j, med, lwr95, upr95, p_pos) |>
  arrange(time, analyte_i, analyte_j) |> 
  print(n = 30)

# Within-type correlation over time (T2 vs. T4 residuals)
fit.s13.post$draws("rho_time", format = "df") |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("rho_time")) |>
  mutate(type = as.integer(gsub("rho_time\\[|\\]", "", name))) |>
  summarise(.by = type,
            med = median(value),
            lwr95 = quantile(value, 0.025),
            upr95 = quantile(value, 0.975)) |>
  left_join(type_lab, by = "type")

# Heatmap of posterior median correlations within each time-point, T2 in
# the lower triangle and T4 in the upper triangle. Types are ordered by
# hierarchical clustering on 1 - |r| (posterior medians averaged over T2 and
# T4), so that correlated types are placed next to each other.
omega_within <- omega_sum |>
  filter(time_i == time_j, type_i != type_j)

r_avg <- omega_within |>
  summarise(.by = c(type_i, type_j), r = mean(med))
R_avg <- diag(K)
R_avg[cbind(r_avg$type_i, r_avg$type_j)] <- r_avg$r

type_ord <- hclust(as.dist(1 - abs(R_avg)), method = "average")$order
analyte_ord <- type_lab$analyte[type_ord]

omega_heatmap <- omega_within |>
  # Keep T2 below and T4 above the diagonal (in the clustered order). The
  # y-axis is reversed, so cells below the diagonal have the column (i)
  # earlier in the order than the row (j).
  filter((time_i == "T2") == (match(type_i, type_ord) < match(type_j, type_ord))) |>
  mutate(credible = lwr95 > 0 | upr95 < 0,
         analyte_i = factor(analyte_i, levels = analyte_ord),
         analyte_j = factor(analyte_j, levels = rev(analyte_ord))) |>
  ggplot(aes(analyte_i, analyte_j, fill = med)) +

                fontface = if_else(credible, "bold", "plain")),
            size = 2.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(limits = c(-1, 1),
                       low = colscale[2],
                       high = colscale[4]) +
  alpha_theme() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank()) +
  labs(fill = "r",
       subtitle = "Lower triangle: T2, upper triangle: T4; bold = 95% CrI excludes 0")

omega_heatmap


# What the correlations do for the burden score: the sign-aligned treatment
# contrasts are correlated in the posterior. Summing draw-by-draw (as in
# burden_eff) carries these covariances; assuming independence does not.
comp_eff <- lapply(1:2, function(t)
  cbind(HDL = -eff(t, type_idx[["HDL"]]), TG = eff(t, type_idx[["TG"]]),
        BP = 0.5 * (eff(t, type_idx[["dias"]]) + eff(t, type_idx[["sys"]])),
        glucose = eff(t, type_idx[["glucose"]]),
        waist = eff(t, type_idx[["waist"]])))
names(comp_eff) <- c("T2", "T4")

# Posterior correlation between the (sign-aligned) component contrasts
lapply(comp_eff, function(x) round(cor(x), 2))

# Posterior SD of the burden contrast, joint vs. assuming independence
sapply(comp_eff, function(x)
  c(sd_joint = sd(rowSums(x) / 5),
    sd_indep = sqrt(sum(apply(x, 2, var))) / 5))
```

## Model expansion: Baseline-dependent treatment effects

```{r}
#| label: moderation-data

# Baseline (T1) omega-3 index of the randomised participants, the moderator
# in s22 (the same data as in models-scripts/model-s22.R)
o3_base <- criteria_dat |>
  distinct(participant) |>
  left_join(AOData::omega3 |>
              filter(time == "T1") |>
              select(participant, omega3index),
            by = "participant")

n_o3_miss <- sum(is.na(o3_base$omega3index))
o3_sd <- sd(o3_base$omega3index, na.rm = TRUE)
```

To assess whether the effect of krill oil supplementation depends on the participants' baseline status, four expansions of model s13 are considered. All keep the full s13 structure (joint imputation of missing pre- and post-intervention values, the multivariate Student's t-likelihood with $\nu = 4$, the time &times; type residual scales and the LKJ correlation matrix) and change only the linear predictor for the expected post-intervention value. In s13, the expected value for participant $p$, measurement type $k$ and post-intervention time-point $t$ is

$$
\begin{align}
\mu_{p,k,t} &= \alpha_{k,t,\text{tx}[p]} + \beta_{k,t}\, x_{p,k} + \beta^{\text{sex}}_{k,t}\, s_p
\end{align}
$$

where $x_{p,k}$ is the standardised pre-intervention value (observed or imputed), $s_p \in \{-0.5, 0.5\}$ codes sex, and $\text{tx}[p] \in \{1, 2\}$ indexes placebo and krill oil, respectively. The treatment effect is the difference between intercepts, $\alpha_{k,t,2} - \alpha_{k,t,1}$, and does not depend on the baseline value. Let $\omega_p = 1$ for participants in the krill oil group and $\omega_p = 0$ for placebo.

**Model s19: treatment &times; own-baseline interaction.** The pre-intervention slope is allowed to differ between treatment groups,

$$
\begin{align}
\mu_{p,k,t} &= \alpha_{k,t,\text{tx}[p]} + \beta_{k,t}\, x_{p,k} + \delta_{k,t}\, \omega_p\, x_{p,k} + \beta^{\text{sex}}_{k,t}\, s_p \\
\delta_{k,t} &= \tau_\delta\, z_{k,t} \\
z_{k,t} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 1) \\
\tau_\delta &\sim \operatorname{Half-Normal}(0, 0.25)
\end{align}
$$

so that the treatment effect for a participant with standardised baseline value $x$ is

$$
\Delta_{k,t}(x) = \alpha_{k,t,2} - \alpha_{k,t,1} + \delta_{k,t}\, x.
$$

Since the outcomes are standardised, the baseline mean is close to zero and the intercept difference keeps its interpretation from s13 as the effect at an average baseline value, while $\delta_{k,t}$ is the change in the treatment effect per SD of the baseline value. The $2K = 24$ interaction terms share a common scale $\tau_\delta$ (non-centred parameterisation), which shrinks individual interactions towards zero unless they are jointly supported by the data. A prior scale of 0.25 places most prior mass on interactions smaller than half an SD of the outcome per SD of baseline.

**Model s20: treatment &times; baseline metabolic burden.** Rather than each outcome's own baseline, s20 uses a single moderator shared across outcomes: a continuous baseline metabolic burden score defined as the mean of the sign-aligned standardised baseline values of the five diagnostic criteria,

$$
\begin{align}
b_p &= \tfrac{1}{5}\left( -x_{p,\text{HDL}} + x_{p,\text{TG}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\left(x_{p,\text{dias}} + x_{p,\text{sys}}\right) + x_{p,\text{glucose}} + x_{p,\text{waist}} \right) \\
\tilde{b}_p &= b_p - \tfrac{1}{N_P} \textstyle\sum_{p'} b_{p'}
\end{align}
$$

where HDL enters with a negative sign so that higher values of $b_p$ indicate worse metabolic health, and blood pressure contributes as the mean of the diastolic and systolic values. The score is computed inside the model from the partly imputed baseline matrix, so it remains a continuous and differentiable function of the imputed values (in contrast to the number of criteria met, or the baseline diagnosis, which are step functions). The linear predictor becomes

$$
\begin{align}
\mu_{p,k,t} &= \alpha_{k,t,\text{tx}[p]} + \beta_{k,t}\, x_{p,k} + \gamma_{k,t}\, \omega_p\, \tilde{b}_p + \beta^{\text{sex}}_{k,t}\, s_p \\
\gamma_{k,t} &= \tau_\gamma\, z_{k,t} \\
z_{k,t} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 1) \\
\tau_\gamma &\sim \operatorname{Half-Normal}(0, 0.25)
\end{align}
$$

with treatment effect $\Delta_{k,t}(\tilde{b}) = \alpha_{k,t,2} - \alpha_{k,t,1} + \gamma_{k,t}\, \tilde{b}$. Centring the burden score on its sample mean keeps the intercept difference interpretable as the effect at average baseline burden.

**Model s21: treatment &times; baseline relative fat mass.** s21 has the same structure as s20, but the shared moderator is the participant's baseline relative fat mass. The moderator is taken from the partly imputed baseline matrix and standardised within each posterior draw to mean 0 and SD 1 over participants,

$$
\begin{align}
f_p &= \frac{x_{p,\text{fat.rel}} - \bar{x}_{\text{fat.rel}}}{\operatorname{SD}(x_{\text{fat.rel}})} \\
\mu_{p,k,t} &= \alpha_{k,t,\text{tx}[p]} + \beta_{k,t}\, x_{p,k} + \gamma_{k,t}\, \omega_p\, f_p + \beta^{\text{sex}}_{k,t}\, s_p
\end{align}
$$

with $\gamma_{k,t}$ given the same partially pooled prior as in s20. The intercept difference is the treatment effect at the average baseline relative fat mass and $\gamma_{k,t}$ is the change in the treatment effect per SD of baseline relative fat mass.

**Model s22: treatment &times; baseline omega-3 index.** In s22 the shared moderator is the baseline red blood cell omega-3 index [@harris2004], which is not one of the modelled outcomes. The index was standardised to mean 0 and SD 1 over participants with an observed baseline value ($o_p$). The baseline index was missing for `r n_o3_miss` participants; these values were imputed in the model with a standard normal prior, $o_p \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 1)$, so that all randomised participants are kept. The linear predictor is

$$
\begin{align}
\mu_{p,k,t} &= \alpha_{k,t,\text{tx}[p]} + \beta_{k,t}\, x_{p,k} + \gamma_{k,t}\, \omega_p\, o_p + \beta^{\text{sex}}_{k,t}\, s_p
\end{align}
$$

with the same partially pooled prior on $\gamma_{k,t}$ as in s20. Here, $\gamma_{k,t}$ is the change in the treatment effect per SD of the baseline omega-3 index (1 SD = `r sprintf("%.2f", o3_sd)` %-points).

**Treatment effects across the moderator.** To show what the interactions imply, treatment effects were predicted from each model at the moderator mean (0) and at &plusmn; 1 SD of the moderator,

$$
\Delta_{k,t}(m) = \alpha_{k,t,2} - \alpha_{k,t,1} + \gamma_{k,t}\, m, \quad m \in \{-\text{SD}, 0, +\text{SD}\},
$$

with $\delta_{k,t}$ in place of $\gamma_{k,t}$ for s19. For s21 and s22 the moderator is standardised, so SD = 1. For s19, the SD is the observed baseline SD of each standardised outcome, and for s20 it is the SD of the centered burden score over participants, computed per posterior draw. Effects are computed per posterior draw and shown on the standardised scale (outcome SD units), where a negative value indicates a lower value with krill oil compared to placebo (@fig-moderation-pred).

All four models had satisfactory chain convergence statistics and effective sample size enabling their use for subsequent inference (@fig-chain-stats-s19s22). 

```{r}
#| label: fig-chain-stats-s19s22
#| fig-cap: "Summary chain statistics (Rhat vs. bulk and tail effective sample size) for the moderation models s19 to s22."
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6

# Parameter summaries, leaving out the data-sized transformed parameters and
# generated quantities (as in the chain diagnostics of previous models)
extract_sum <- function(fit) {
  all_vars <- fit$metadata()$variables
  keep <- setdiff(
    all_vars,
    grep("^(lp__|y|y_rep|y_expect|y_impute|pre|pre_impute|pre_wide|y_wide_1|y_wide_2|mu_wide_1|mu_wide_2|mu|sig|log_lik|log_lik_part|diagnosed|n_criteria)\\[",
         all_vars, value = TRUE)
  )
  fit$summary(variables = keep, .cores = 12)
}

# Extracting chain diagnostics takes some time, the summaries are stored in
# data-derived/ and re-computed when refit.models == TRUE or the file is missing.
chain_sum_file <- "data-derived/ch-07-chain-diagnostics-s19-s22.RDS"

if (!file.exists(chain_sum_file) || refit.models) {
  chain_sums <- lapply(paste0("s", 19:22), function(m) {
    fit <- readRDS(sprintf("fits/paper1/fit.%s.post.RDS", m))
    extract_sum(fit) |> mutate(model = m)
  })
  saveRDS(chain_sums, chain_sum_file)
} else {
  chain_sums <- readRDS(chain_sum_file)
}

bind_rows(chain_sums) |>
  filter(variable != "lp__",
         !is.na(rhat)) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = paste0("s", 19:22))) |>

  ggplot(aes(ess_bulk, rhat, size = ess_tail)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = colscale[6]) +
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  alpha_theme() +
  labs(x = "Effective sample size (ESS Bulk)",
       y = "Rhat",
       size = "ESS tail")
```





```{r}
#| label: fig-moderation-pred
#| fig-cap: "Predicted treatment effects (krill oil - placebo) at the moderator mean and at &plusmn; 1 SD of the moderator in models s19 (each outcome's own baseline value), s20 (baseline metabolic burden score), s21 (baseline relative fat mass) and s22 (baseline omega-3 index), after the supplementation and combined periods. Points and error bars show posterior medians with 50% and 95% CrI on the standardised scale (outcome SD units)."
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-width: 7

# Predicted treatment effects at the moderator mean and +/- 1 SD. Reading the
# fits takes some time, the summaries are stored in data-derived/ and are
# re-computed when refit.models == TRUE or the file is missing.
mod_pred_file <- "data-derived/ch-07-moderation-pred.RDS"
mod_burden_file <- "data-derived/ch-07-moderation-burden.RDS"
mod_coef_file <- "data-derived/ch-07-moderation-coef.RDS"

# (also re-computed if the stored coefficient summary predates the
# P(benefit) column)
if (!file.exists(mod_pred_file) || !file.exists(mod_burden_file) ||
    !file.exists(mod_coef_file) ||
    !"benefit" %in% names(readRDS(mod_coef_file)) || refit.models) {

  # Observed baseline SD of each standardised outcome (moderator SD in s19)
  pre_sd <- dat$dat |>
    filter(pre_miss == 1) |>
    distinct(P, type, pre_obs) |>
    summarise(.by = type, mod_sd = sd(pre_obs))

  # Intercept difference alpha[t, k, 2] - alpha[t, k, 1] and the interaction
  # coefficient par[k, t] (coef) per draw
  effect_draws <- function(fit, par) {
    a <- fit$draws("alpha", format = "df") |>
      select(.draw, starts_with("alpha")) |>
      pivot_longer(cols = -.draw, values_to = "alpha") |>
      mutate(name = gsub("alpha\\[|\\]", "", name)) |>
      separate(name, into = c("time", "type", "treat"), sep = ",", convert = TRUE) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = treat, values_from = alpha, names_prefix = "a") |>
      mutate(diff = a2 - a1) |>
      select(.draw, time, type, diff)

    g <- fit$draws(par, format = "df") |>
      select(.draw, starts_with(par)) |>
      pivot_longer(cols = -.draw, values_to = "coef") |>
      mutate(name = gsub(paste0(par, "\\[|\\]"), "", name)) |>
      separate(name, into = c("type", "time"), sep = ",", convert = TRUE)

    inner_join(a, g, by = c(".draw", "time", "type"))
  }

  fit <- readRDS("fits/paper1/fit.s19.post.RDS")
  eff19 <- effect_draws(fit, "delta") |>
    inner_join(pre_sd, by = "type") |>
    mutate(model = "s19")

  # s20: SD of the centred burden score over participants, per draw
  fit <- readRDS("fits/paper1/fit.s20.post.RDS")
  burden_sd <- fit$draws("burden_c", format = "matrix")
  burden_sd <- data.frame(.draw = seq_len(nrow(burden_sd)),
                          mod_sd = apply(burden_sd, 1, sd))
  eff20 <- effect_draws(fit, "gamma") |>
    inner_join(burden_sd, by = ".draw") |>
    mutate(model = "s20")

  # s21 and s22: standardised moderators (SD = 1)
  fit <- readRDS("fits/paper1/fit.s21.post.RDS")
  eff21 <- effect_draws(fit, "gamma") |> mutate(mod_sd = 1, model = "s21")

  fit <- readRDS("fits/paper1/fit.s22.post.RDS")
  eff22 <- effect_draws(fit, "gamma") |> mutate(mod_sd = 1, model = "s22")
  rm(fit)

  mod_eff <- bind_rows(eff19, eff20, eff21, eff22) |>
    expand_grid(m = c(-1, 0, 1)) |>
    mutate(effect = diff + coef * m * mod_sd)

  # Burden score effect per draw, combined from the criteria as in
  # joint-burden-score: (-HDL + TG + 0.5 * (dias + sys) + glucose + waist) / 5
  burden_w <- data.frame(
    type = unname(type_idx[c("HDL", "TG", "dias", "sys", "glucose", "waist")]),
    w = c(-1, 1, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1) / 5)

  mod_burden <- mod_eff |>
    inner_join(burden_w, by = "type") |>
    summarise(.by = c(model, time, m, .draw), effect = sum(w * effect)) |>
    summarise(.by = c(model, time, m),
              med = median(effect),
              lwr95 = quantile(effect, 0.025),
              upr95 = quantile(effect, 0.975),
              lwr50 = quantile(effect, 0.25),
              upr50 = quantile(effect, 0.75),
              p_neg = mean(effect < 0))

  saveRDS(mod_burden, mod_burden_file)

  # Moderation parameter per SD of the moderator (coef * mod_sd) for each
  # outcome, and for the burden score (type = NA) combined per draw
  coef_draws <- bind_rows(eff19, eff20, eff21, eff22) |>
    mutate(coef_sd = coef * mod_sd) |>
    select(.draw, model, time, type, coef_sd)

  # HDL and adiponectin are beneficial when increased (as in contrast-text),
  # the burden score is already sign-aligned
  up_benefit <- unname(type_idx[c("HDL", "Adiponectin")])

  mod_coef <- coef_draws |>
    inner_join(burden_w, by = "type") |>
    summarise(.by = c(model, time, .draw), coef_sd = sum(w * coef_sd)) |>
    mutate(type = NA_integer_) |>
    bind_rows(coef_draws) |>
    summarise(.by = c(model, time, type),
              med = median(coef_sd),
              lwr95 = quantile(coef_sd, 0.025),
              upr95 = quantile(coef_sd, 0.975),
              lwr50 = quantile(coef_sd, 0.25),
              upr50 = quantile(coef_sd, 0.75),
              # Probability that the treatment effect at +1 SD of the
              # moderator is more beneficial than at the moderator mean
              benefit = mean(if_else(type %in% up_benefit, -coef_sd, coef_sd) < 0))

  saveRDS(mod_coef, mod_coef_file)

  mod_pred <- mod_eff |>
    summarise(.by = c(model, time, type, m),
              med = median(effect),
              lwr95 = quantile(effect, 0.025),
              upr95 = quantile(effect, 0.975),
              lwr50 = quantile(effect, 0.25),
              upr50 = quantile(effect, 0.75),
              p_neg = mean(effect < 0))

  saveRDS(mod_pred, mod_pred_file)

} else {
  mod_pred <- readRDS(mod_pred_file)
  mod_burden <- readRDS(mod_burden_file)
  mod_coef <- readRDS(mod_coef_file)
}


mod_pred |>
  inner_join(labels, by = "type") |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(label, levels = labels$label[match(levels(pred_plot_dat$analyte),
                                                      labels$analyte)]),
    model = factor(model,
                   levels = c("s19", "s20", "s21", "s22"),
                   labels = c("s19: Own baseline", "s20: Metabolic burden",
                              "s21: Relative fat mass", "s22: Omega-3 index")),
    m = factor(m, levels = c(-1, 0, 1), labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")),
    time = factor(time, levels = c(1, 2),
                  labels = c("Supplementation", "Combined"))) |>

  ggplot(aes(m, med, color = time, group = time)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2, color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr95, ymax = upr95),
                width = 0, linewidth = 0.4,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr50, ymax = upr50),
                width = 0, linewidth = 1,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  facet_grid(label ~ model, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(label = label_wrap_gen(14),
                                 model = label_wrap_gen(14))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(3, 6)]) +
  alpha_theme(text_base_size = 7) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0)) +
  labs(y = "Treatment effect, krill oil - placebo (outcome SD units)")
```


Combining the predicted effects on the diagnostic criteria per posterior draw, in the same way as for the metabolic burden score in s13, gives the predicted treatment effect on the burden score across each moderator (@fig-moderation-burden).


```{r}
#| label: fig-moderation-burden
#| fig-cap: "Predicted treatment effects (krill oil - placebo) on the metabolic burden score at the moderator mean and at &plusmn; 1 SD of the moderator in models s19 (each outcome's own baseline value), s20 (baseline metabolic burden score), s21 (baseline relative fat mass) and s22 (baseline omega-3 index), after the supplementation and combined periods. The burden score effect is combined per posterior draw from the effects on the diagnostic criteria. Points and error bars show posterior medians with 50% and 95% CrI on the standardised scale (SD units)."
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-width: 7

mod_burden |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model,
                   levels = c("s19", "s20", "s21", "s22"),
                   labels = c("s19: Own baseline", "s20: Metabolic burden",
                              "s21: Relative fat mass", "s22: Omega-3 index")),
    m = factor(m, levels = c(-1, 0, 1), labels = c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")),
    time = factor(time, levels = c(1, 2),
                  labels = c("Supplementation", "Combined"))) |>

  ggplot(aes(m, med, color = time, group = time)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2, color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr95, ymax = upr95),
                width = 0, linewidth = 0.4,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lwr50, ymax = upr50),
                width = 0, linewidth = 1,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  facet_grid(. ~ model) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(3, 6)]) +
  alpha_theme(text_base_size = 7) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(y = "Average burden score<br>Krill oil - Placebo (SD-units)")
```


The moderation parameters of all outcomes and the burden score are summarised in @tbl-moderation-coef.


```{r}
#| label: tbl-moderation-coef
#| tbl-cap: "Moderation parameters, the change in the treatment effect (krill oil - placebo) per SD of the moderator, in models s19 (each outcome's own baseline value, $\\delta_{k,t}$), s20 (baseline metabolic burden score, $\\gamma_{k,t}$), s21 (baseline relative fat mass, $\\gamma_{k,t}$) and s22 (baseline omega-3 index, $\\gamma_{k,t}$), after the supplementation and combined periods. The burden score parameter is combined per posterior draw from the parameters of the diagnostic criteria. Values are posterior medians with 50% and 95% CrI on the standardised scale (SD units). P(benefit) is the posterior probability that the treatment effect at +1 SD of the moderator is more beneficial than at the moderator mean (higher values for HDL and adiponectin, lower values otherwise)."

score_levels <- c(labels$label[match(levels(pred_plot_dat$analyte), labels$analyte)],
                  "Metabolic burden score")

mod_coef |>
  left_join(labels, by = "type") |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(replace_na(label, "Metabolic burden score"), levels = score_levels),
    model = factor(model,
                   levels = c("s19", "s20", "s21", "s22"),
                   labels = c("s19: Own baseline", "s20: Metabolic burden",
                              "s21: Relative fat mass", "s22: Omega-3 index")),
    est = sprintf("%.2f", med),
    ci50 = sprintf("%.2f, %.2f", lwr50, upr50),
    ci95 = sprintf("%.2f, %.2f", lwr95, upr95),
    prob = fmt_prob(benefit)) |>
  select(model, label, time, est, ci50, ci95, prob) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = c(est, ci50, ci95, prob)) |>
  arrange(model, label) |>
  select(model, label, est_1, ci50_1, ci95_1, prob_1, est_2, ci50_2, ci95_2, prob_2) |>
  group_by(model) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Supplementation", columns = c(est_1, ci50_1, ci95_1, prob_1)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Combined", columns = c(est_2, ci50_2, ci95_2, prob_2)) |>
  cols_label(
    label = "",
    est_1 = "Median", ci50_1 = "50% CrI", ci95_1 = "95% CrI", prob_1 = "P(benefit)",
    est_2 = "Median", ci50_2 = "50% CrI", ci95_2 = "95% CrI", prob_2 = "P(benefit)")
```
